note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

MEASURED, NOT COMPUTED, and not hand-merged: the baseline itself was regenerated by `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` on the merged tree. TWO trees were analysed in ONE environment by the same scripts/route-graph.mjs, with the companion extension fleet cloned PINNED exactly as CI clones it (116/116, missingCount 0 on every route of both trees). The default branch alone at fbe9df77e423c49e8c64796bc7a5456c9b0fbac5 lands EXACTLY on its four committed ceilings - /api/mcp 1768, /chat 1870, /api/a2a 1776, /api/llm-bridge 1786 - and the merged tree measures each of them plus ONE. The reachable sets were diffed module by module: on all four routes the whole growth is the SAME single first-party module, src/lib/artifacts/artifact-revision-append.ts, and NOTHING leaves any route's reachable set. That module is the change road's revision writer - the transaction a Regenerate needs to append the corrected revision of the artifact under review and to re-file a producing run's output onto it. The default branch owns a copy of this file (its mid-run same-artifact append, cinatra#3030 W6), but reaches it from these four routes through no static edge; this branch adds two static ones, packages/agents/src/lifecycle-repair-producer-completion-store.ts and src/lib/blog-post-artifact-materializer.ts, both on the producer-completion seam all four extension-aware routes already reach. It cannot be narrowed away honestly: each edge is a single named import of one function, and the alternatives are to inline the transaction into its callers or to reach it through a specifier the scanner cannot read, both of which hide the growth rather than remove it. /sign-in takes nothing from this branch: it measures 163 on the merged tree, far below the ceiling the default branch committed, so the regeneration ratchets it DOWN to what it measures and retires the record whose ceiling moved - a shrink, never a raise.
